OFFICIAL WARNING MAPS

Weather & fire alerts

Official Queensland maps are displayed below, with their own current warning details. Select Moreton Island or zoom to the island. These statewide maps can be delayed and are not a guarantee that your location is safe.

Weather warnings · Queensland Government · allow up to five minutes for source updates.

Blank or blocked map? Open the official warning service ↗. A blank map does not mean there are no warnings.

Weather warnings

Read the warning area, issue time, expected conditions and recommended actions. Marine forecasts and warnings may differ between the sheltered bay and ocean coast.

BOM warnings summary ↗

Fire warning levels

Advice: stay informed. Watch and Act: conditions threaten safety; act on the warning. Emergency Warning: take the protective action specified immediately. Incident points indicate general locations, not fire boundaries.

Queensland Fire Department ↗

Fire bans & park rules

A lack of incidents does not mean fires are allowed. Check current fire bans and park restrictions separately before lighting a campfire. Call 000 to report a fire or immediate emergency.

Current fire bans ↗
CHECK BEFORE EVERY OUTING

Tides & conditions

Tides, wind and access change your plans. Use the map’s time control for tide predictions and weather/marine forecast indicators. Official services provide additional conditions and warnings.

Beach driving

Avoid driving within two hours either side of high tide, and longer where local conditions require. Even low tide does not guarantee access. Check the current park conditions report and the tide reference it specifies.

Read Queensland Parks driving guidance ↗
VISITOR INFORMATION

Island guide

DATA CATALOGUE & PROVENANCE

Data catalogue

Map coordinates use WGS 84 / UTM zone 56S (EPSG:32756), with easting and northing in metres. GeoJSON downloads retain standard WGS84 longitude/latitude geometry; select EPSG:32756 in QGIS to view or export them in UTM. Extracts include features intersecting the island’s surrounding area; some geometries extend beyond it.

Terrain services

Hillshade is rendered from Queensland’s multi-source elevation service: resolution and survey date vary. LiDAR footprints show the 2009 Brisbane survey and an incomplete 2025 bathymetry project intersecting the selected area. Contours switch from 10 m SRTM to 5 m and 1 m LiDAR at close zoom; a blank layer may indicate scale or coverage limits.

Contour metadata · Elevation service metadata

More mapping resources

Coverage & accuracy

Only source-backed place reference points are displayed. Other entries retain their descriptions without map pins; null geometry in downloads means location withheld. Reference points are not campsite boundaries. This edition has no numbered campsite footprints, verified facility-point layer, live road closures, bathymetric navigation chart or offline basemap. GIS source dates differ from the download date. Marine habitat is the published 2008 dataset. Zero-feature extracts mean no features were returned within the selected extent, not an assurance of absence. Data attribution: © State of Queensland. Check source metadata and licensing before reuse. Marine designated areas overlap zoning; inspect both.
